1	# claudinite-tasks — scheduled work
2	
3	Everything whose subject is task work: the work-item queue, the executor, the task contract and
4	its signals, calendar/anchor math, run records, code-work, and the delivery lane a task's output
5	lands through. Declaring this pack is what gives a repo scheduled work; a repo that does not
6	declare it runs none, which is a supported state rather than a degraded one.
7	
8	The mechanism itself, from the state machine and the generator to the executor's protocol,
9	urgency, forcing and recovery, is [`docs/PRINCIPLES.md`](docs/PRINCIPLES.md); authoring a task is
10	the `writing-tasks` skill's subject. This file is the pack's own map.
11	
12	## Layout
13	
14	Every module sits in the ROLE it plays, and the graph between the roles is
15	one-directional. `contract/` and `items/` are what everything agrees on and name no
16	stage; `world/` holds the only modules that reach outside the run; the stages sit on
17	top of those and never import each other sideways or upwards. The `tasks-stage-barriers`
18	and `tasks-world-edges-live-in-world` checks are what hold the shape.
19	
20	| Path | The role |
21	|---|---|
22	| `src/contract/` | what a task DECLARES and what its declaration means: the declaration's shape and defaults, the term vocabulary and the precondition seam every caller asks through, cadence and anchor arithmetic, the auto-merge policy engine, task discovery, dormancy |
23	| `src/items/` | the work item as DATA, over the vocabulary and grammar `public/` defines: the queue listings, the run record, the pick order over the open queue, the heartbeat |
24	| `src/world/` | the only outward edges, each a named port — `github.mjs` (every REST path this pack calls, as a named operation), `actions.mjs` (the runner's environment) with `hold.mjs` and the three env bags beside it, `sessions.mjs` (the routine fire that starts an agent), `git.mjs`, `processes.mjs`, `clock.mjs` |
25	| `src/signals/` | the collectors a precondition is handed, read through the ports and described in the contract's terms |
26	| `src/schedule/` | the tick: the repair phase that runs first, then which declared tasks have a window open and the items filed for them |
27	| `src/execute/` | the executor: claiming a ready item, running its code-work, handing it to an agent session |
28	| `src/session/` | what runs INSIDE a work-item session: converging the item, verifying its outcome, the exec record, dispatch resolution, and the automerge verdict as a command |
29	| `src/deliver/` | turning a run's output into a landed pull request or a regenerated file |
30	| `src/recover/` | repair: the queue's repair rules, workflow-failure escalation, the dead-run continuation |
31	| `src/adopt/` | what an adopting repo receives: the workflows converged from the stubs, the per-repo cron minute |
32	| `queue/` | `tasks/implement-request/`, the engine's own built-in task; the spec is `public/implement-request.md` |
33	| `stubs/` | the two workflow files an adopting repo receives |
34	| `public/` | **everything outside this pack may reference** — the vocabulary and grammar `src/` builds on, the import surface, and the documents a routine reads. See below |
35	| `tasks/` | this pack's own tasks: `usage-fold` (it folds this mechanism's run records and outcome labels), `tasks-usage-fold` (what the machinery itself cost - runs, billed minutes, API calls, outcomes, parks, latencies) and `verify-production` (coded production validations - URL probes judged as code-work) |
36	| `worldRules/` | the task-declaration checks |
37	| `workRules/` | the armed-auto-merge gate (`automerge-policy-scope`) |
38	| `declared-checks.json` | `tasks-pack-read-through-its-surface` — the guard over this pack's published surface, which runs wherever the pack is declared |
39	| `test/` | the unit suite, mirroring `src/`, and `test/sim/` — the simulator and its scenario suite, the mechanism's executable spec |
40	| `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` | the mechanism as claims, each citing the test that proves it |
41	| `src/deliver/deliver-pr.md` | the landing procedure every PR-delivering task's worker is pointed at, beside the lane it describes |
42	
43	## `public/` — everything outside this pack may reference
44	
45	One folder, one promise: **a name in `public/` does not move.** Everything a routine reads, another
46	pack imports or a member's own local pack names lives here, and nothing else of this pack is
47	addressable from outside. A member's `.github/workflows/` runs the entry points under `src/`
48	named by the two stubs, which are this pack's own files and not an outside caller.
49	
50	Another pack's code may import `packs/claudinite-tasks/public/*` and nothing else of this pack;
51	the `pack-independence` barrier's allow list names that directory, and no other pack gains an
52	equivalent surface by existing. **A member's own `.claudinite/local/packs/**` reads it the same
53	way**, through its mount (`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/public/*`): the nightly
54	converge replaces `.claudinite/shared/` and may never touch a member's own packs, so an import
55	aimed anywhere else is one this repository cannot repair when the layout behind it moves.
56	
57	### Documents named from outside
58	
59	| Path | What names it |
60	|---|---|
61	| `instructions.md` | a repo's work-item routine, as a stored prompt in its console settings |
62	| `implement-request.md` | the machine block of every issue adopted into the queue |
63	
64	### Modules other packs import
65	
66	Three of the five are the DEFINITION, and `src/` imports them from here: the vocabulary, the
67	grammar over it and the GitHub client import nothing of `src/`. The other two are the
68	machinery's own operations under a stable name.
69	
70	| Module | What it publishes |
71	|---|---|
72	| `task-constants.mjs` | every value the queue writes and reads: the work item's labels, markers and body fields, the leases, the commit trailers, the declaration defaults, the pack's own parameters, the two workflow file names |
73	| `work-item-grammar.mjs` | the parse and serialize over that vocabulary — the title grammar that is an item's identity, the status and outcome decode over its labels (every legacy spelling included), the body fields, the machine block, the commit trailer |
74	| `github.mjs` | the GitHub client (`makeGh` and the run's call count), `dispatchWorkflow`, and the tracker issue a recurring task logs every run to |
75	| `delivery.mjs` | `deliverGenerated` — a regenerated file landed on a pull request that lands itself — and the landing lane's five names for a worker that lands its own pull request |
76	| `task-declaration.mjs` | the declaration's executable contract: the loader, its validation, the precondition evaluator the executor runs at pick, and the auto-merge policy engine |
77	
78	A module publishes **named** exports rather than `export *`. A consumer needing something absent
79	asks for the named export to be added here, never a deeper import, which
80	`tasks-pack-read-through-its-surface` refuses. Who reads each name
81	is derived on demand: `node packs/claudinite-canon-curation/pack-surface.mjs packs/claudinite-tasks`
82	renders the surface and its consumers from the tree.
83	
84	A pack whose **non-task** code reads any of the modules above declares `requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`. A
85	pack's `tasks/` folder needs no declaration: a mount without this pack carries no `tasks/` at all,
86	since a task folder is inert without the queue that runs it.
87	
88	## Adoption
89	
90	The two workflow files and the routine endpoints cannot converge into place — `.github/workflows/`
91	is the one directory a member's nightly update may never write — so they are scaffolded once, at
92	adoption, by the `adopt-pack` skill. They are static from then on: the per-repo cron minute and
93	anchor hours are written once, secrets travel as one fixed line, and the `run:` lines name mount
94	pack paths behind which everything updates nightly.
95	
96	## Checks
97	
98	| Rule | Confidence | Dimension | Enforcement |
99	|---|---|---|---|
100	| `task-declaration-shape` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
101	| `task-code-work-env` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
102	| `automerge-policy-scope` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
103	| `executor-workflow-secrets` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
104	| `tasks-pack-read-through-its-surface` | high | correctness | declared check: blocking |
105	| `repo-variables-through-the-bag` | high | correctness | declared check: blocking |
106	| `issue-label-outside-the-queue-vocabulary` | high | correctness | declared check: blocking |
107	| `queue-mark-named-literally` | high | correctness | declared check: blocking |
108	
109	`tasks-pack-read-through-its-surface` is this pack's, not the canon's, because the consumers that
110	can get it wrong are members: it scans a repo's own `packs/` **and** its `.claudinite/local/packs/`,
111	the tree no converge may rewrite, so a deep import written there is caught in that repo's own run
112	rather than when it crashes.
113	
114	`repo-variables-through-the-bag` — a module reads a repository variable over the REST variables
115	API, which the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` is refused on in every member (403, and no `permissions:` key
116	grants it), so the read never answers. Every repository variable already travels in the executor's
117	vars bag: a task's code-work finds it in `process.env`, engine code reads `varsBag(env)`.
118	
119	The first two are relevance-first — inert until the repo carries a `tasks/<name>/task.json` of its own; the third is self-gating on the branch's own arming trailer.
120	
121	- `task-declaration-shape` — a task declaration the scheduler reads is incomplete or illegal — no `trigger` saying who mints an occurrence, an unknown condition, an illegal value — so the task never fires or fires wrong.
122	- `task-code-work-env` — a task reads a `CLAUDINITE_*` variable code-work never sets, so a parameter (a scope filter, a dry-run switch) silently never arrives and the run goes green in its most dangerous mode.
123	- `executor-workflow-secrets` — the executor workflow does not pass a secret the tasks of this repo's packs declare, so the queue picks the item up and only the run finds out the secret is not there. The list is the tasks' alone; an invocation endpoint's `tokenSecret` is config, stamped by `converge-workflows.mjs` and reported by the invocation call itself. Advisory because the remedy is a human-merged PR to `.github/workflows/`, the one fix a member's own machinery cannot make.
124	- `issue-label-outside-the-queue-vocabulary`: an `issue_write` call applies a label outside the `task:` namespace, which no scheduler run, executor or janitor reads: the issue is filed as if something would pick it up. `task:origin:ad-hoc` asks the queue for the work; no label at all is the ordinary issue.
125	- `queue-mark-named-literally`: a pack's prose tells a session to mark an issue for the queue, or to tag a backlog issue, without naming the label; naming `task:origin:ad-hoc` on the line satisfies it.
126	- `automerge-policy-scope` — a branch that stamped the `Claudinite-Automerge-Policy` trailer (its run intends to land its own PR) carries a diff its declared policy does not cover, which is exactly the unreviewed change the policy exists to stop.
127

1	// The tasks the ENGINE itself ships (docs/PRINCIPLES.md), as opposed to
2	// the ones a declared pack contributes. There is exactly one: `implement-request`,
3	// the task a marked issue's work item names.
4	//
5	// It is a TASK rather than a special item shape because that is what keeps the
6	// request mode from being a second mechanism — the item's first body line is a task
7	// path validated in code like every other, the same-title mutex serializes twin
8	// requests, the repair phase's leashes cover it, `verify-outcome` polices its ceiling and
9	// `record-exec` counts it. What follows from it being engine-owned rather than
10	// pack-owned is exactly two things, and they live here: task discovery gains this
11	// root beside the pack scan, and the validated task-path shape gains its form.
12	//
13	// It is not a pack and declares nothing. Wherever the queue runs it is active,
14	// which is also what fences the one field only it may declare
15	// (`model_from_request`): no pack can opt itself in, because no pack can be this.
16	
17	import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
18	import { dirname, join, relative, sep } from 'node:path';
19	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
20	
21	// The id the built-in task's work items are titled with — `engine/implement-request`
22	// — in the same `<pack>/<task>` grammar as everything else, so nothing downstream

51	// block is written into an issue body, which this repository can never rewrite, so

1	// Is this project's SCHEDULER dormant? A project goes dormant when it is finished,
2	// parked, or simply not being worked on: it should stop paying the upkeep of a project
3	// that IS being worked on.
4	//
5	// WHY THIS LIVES IN THIS PACK. Every effect dormancy has is an effect on the queue —
6	// nothing is instantiated, nothing is picked up, and nothing outside expects movement.
7	// A repo that declares no tasks pack has no scheduler at all, so the word means nothing
8	// there, and an engine that validated it for such a repo was answering for a mechanism
9	// it does not own. So the setting is one of this pack's parameters, declared where the
10	// pack is:
11	//
12	//   { "id": "claudinite-tasks", "config": { "dormant": true } }
13	//
14	// What dormancy means, exactly — it is narrow on purpose:
15	//   - NO RECURRING WORK. The vendored scheduler stops before it evaluates a
16	//     precondition, so no work item is instantiated, no agent session is started, and
17	//     no maintenance PR is opened. Nothing scheduled runs "for nothing" on a repo
18	//     nobody is working on.
19	//   - NO UPKEEP CEREMONY FROM OUTSIDE. Whatever looks at this repo from the outside
20	//     reads the same declaration and asks it nothing about its upkeep: neither its
21	//     scheduler nor its mount is judged, and no fleet-wide operation is run against it
22	//     (owner, 2026-09-13). A scheduler TOLD to stop must not then be nagged for
23	//     stopping, and a mount nothing will converge cannot be behind in a way anyone is
24	//     going to fix — both verdicts would be findings with no owner. What a reader owes
25	//     such a repo instead is the word "dormant" where those verdicts would have sat.
26	//   - EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS ON. Claudinite is not switched off: the session hooks, the
27	//     checks engine, the mounted skills and pack prose all work exactly as before the
28	//     moment someone opens a session on the repo. Dormancy is about unattended upkeep,
29	//     never about what an interactive session may do.
30	//
31	// ONE PREDICATE, EVERY SHAPE. It reads a raw parsed .claudinite-settings.json and the
32	// normalized config `loadConfig` returns, because a cross-repo reader fetches another
33	// repo's declaration over the API with no engine loaded against that tree and must
34	// decide dormancy by the same test that repo's own scheduler used. A second notion of
35	// dormancy would nag exactly the repos that had already opted out.
36	//
37	// Import-light and free of `node:` on purpose: the dashboard page reads this in the
38	// browser through the pack's published public/, and a `node:` import anywhere in
39	// that graph blocks the page's first module load.
40	import { RENAMED_PACKS } from '../../../../engine/pack_loader/renamed-packs.mjs';
41	import { TASKS_PACK_ID, DORMANT_CONFIG_KEY } from '../../public/task-constants.mjs';
42	
43	export { TASKS_PACK_ID };
44	
45	// A declared id as it resolves today. A member's declaration can carry a spelling from
46	// before a rename, and the config of a pack a member writes into its own repo must keep
47	// resolving under every spelling it was ever written under.
48	const resolves = (id) => typeof id === 'string' && (RENAMED_PACKS[id] ?? id) === TASKS_PACK_ID;
49	
50	// This pack's parameters, from whichever shape the caller holds.
51	//
52	// The normalized view first: `loadConfig` folds every entry's `config` into `packConfig`
53	// keyed by the pack's own id, so a scheduler that already loaded its settings needs no
54	// second walk. Then the raw declaration, where the parameters sit on the entry object as
55	// the member wrote them — which is all a cross-repo reader ever has.
56	function packParameters(config) {
57	  if (config === null || typeof config !== 'object') return undefined;
58	  const folded = config.packConfig?.[TASKS_PACK_ID];
59	  if (folded !== null && typeof folded === 'object') return folded;
60	  for (const entry of Array.isArray(config.packs) ? config.packs : []) {
61	    if (entry !== null && typeof entry === 'object' && resolves(entry.id)) return entry.config;
62	  }
63	  return undefined;
64	}
65	
66	// What the declaration says, before any judgement about whether it says it legally.
67	// `undefined` means the project never answered, which is the normal shape and means awake.
68	function declared(config) {
69	  if (config === null || typeof config !== 'object') return undefined;
70	  const own = packParameters(config)?.[DORMANT_CONFIG_KEY];
71	  if (own !== undefined) return own;
72	  // The retired spelling, underneath the pack entry so a converged member is never
73	  // overridden by a stale key its migration left behind. `raw` is the declaration as
74	  // the member wrote it, which is where a top-level key survives now that the engine
75	  // no longer normalizes one it does not own.
76	  // @legacy-tolerance advisory:legacy-shape-in-use retire:#1846
77	  return config.raw?.[DORMANT_CONFIG_KEY] ?? config[DORMANT_CONFIG_KEY];
78	}
79	
80	// The predicate. Strictly `=== true`, so every malformed value below reads as awake —
81	// the conservative direction, since the alternative is silently stopping a project's
82	// entire scheduled workload on a typo.
83	export const isDormant = (config) => declared(config) === true;
84	
85	// The settings errors this parameter can carry, in the `{ what, fix }` shape the world
86	// runner collects. A string "true", a `{ since }` object or a reason left in its place
87	// would all read as dormant to a truthiness test and as awake to the predicate above,
88	// and the difference is a whole repo's scheduled work — so the wrong TYPE is reported
89	// rather than coerced. The pack owns this because the pack owns the parameter.
90	export function dormancyErrors(config) {
91	  const value = declared(config);
92	  if (value === undefined || typeof value === 'boolean') return [];
93	  return [{
94	    what: `"${DORMANT_CONFIG_KEY}" on the "${TASKS_PACK_ID}" pack entry must be true or false, got ${JSON.stringify(value)}`,
95	    fix: `set it to true to stop this project's recurring work, or remove it — e.g. { "id": "${TASKS_PACK_ID}", "config": { "dormant": true } }`,
96	  }];
97	}

1	// THE CLOCK PORT. Reading "now" is an edge to the world exactly like a REST call
2	// is: it makes a run's answer depend on something outside its inputs. Every
3	// module under `src/` that needs the current instant asks here, so a simulator
4	// can drive a whole run at a chosen instant by replacing this one implementation
5	// and nothing else changes hands.
6	//
7	// Parsing a timestamp is NOT a clock read — `new Date(iso)` over a string a
8	// caller supplied is arithmetic, stays where it is used, and is deliberately
9	// outside what this port covers.
10	
11	// What "now" currently reads from. The wall clock in production, and whatever a
12	// simulator installed while it is driving a run.
13	let readMs = () => Date.now();
14	
15	// The current instant, as a Date. The one place `new Date()` is called with no
16	// argument anywhere under `src/`.
17	export const now = () => new Date(readMs());
18	
19	// The current instant in epoch milliseconds — for durations and unique suffixes,
20	// where a Date object would only be unwrapped again.
21	export const nowMs = () => readMs();
22	
23	// The current instant as the ISO-8601 string the queue's records are written in.
24	export const nowIso = () => new Date(readMs()).toISOString();
25	
26	// Replace the reading, and return the undo. This is the "replacing this one
27	// implementation" the header promises: a harness running the engine against a
28	// virtual clock installs its own instant here, and every `src/` module that asks
29	// for the time — the claim comment's stamp, a `Woken:` field, a minted branch's
30	// date — answers in that world rather than in this year.
31	//
32	// Deliberately a whole-process switch rather than a threaded argument: the point
33	// of a port is that a caller says what it needs and not where it comes from, and
34	// threading an instant through every module that reads one would put the clock
35	// back into every signature this module exists to keep it out of. Production
36	// never calls it; the undo is what keeps one harness's instant out of the next.
37	export function installClock(read) {
38	  const previous = readMs;
39	  readMs = read;
40	  return () => { readMs = previous; };
41	}

1	// THE PICK ORDER over the open queue — which ready item a worker takes next, and
2	// which ones it must skip. It sits with the items rather than with either caller
3	// because BOTH stages ask it: the executor to choose what to claim, and the
4	// scheduler run to count what is pickable before it spends an executor invocation
5	// on an empty queue.
6	//
7	// The order (docs/PRINCIPLES.md): urgent first, then RANDOM among the ready, with
8	// two skip rules read live at pick time. Random rather than oldest-first because
9	// nothing leans on FIFO aging — the stale-ready escalation is period-scale — while
10	// a deterministic order lets one unlucky head dominate every run of a chain.
11	//
12	//  - SAME-TITLE MUTEX (S15/F6): skip an item whose exact title has another open
13	//    item executing or handed to an agent — one task, one execution at a time,
14	//    while a fan-out's distinct qualifiers still parallelize.
15	//  - THE `after` YIELD (S23): skip a scheduled item whose task declares `after:
16	//    [T]` while T's standing item is live THIS CYCLE (ready / executing / agent).
17	//    A declined upstream holds nothing back — it has no item at all (a no files
18	//    nothing, PRINCIPLES.md) — and neither does one sitting `needs-human`: a broken
19	//    upstream must not halt its dependents indefinitely.
20	
21	import {
22	  URGENT, STATUS_READY, STATUS_RUNNING_EXECUTOR, STATUS_RUNNING_AGENT,
23	} from '../../public/task-constants.mjs';
24	import {
25	  isStatus, parseWorkItemTitle, parseWorkItemBody, isStandingItem, hasLabel,
26	} from '../../public/work-item-grammar.mjs';
27	
28	export const titleOf = (item) => (item.title ?? '').trim();
29	// An item somebody is executing — the executor holds it, or the agent it handed to
30	// does. Decoded, never a literal label test: the item may wear any engine's spelling.
31	export const running = (item) => isStatus(item, STATUS_RUNNING_EXECUTOR) || isStatus(item, STATUS_RUNNING_AGENT);
32	// WHICH TASK AN ITEM NAMES. A filed `[claudinite-work]` item says so in its title;
33	// a marked issue (PRINCIPLES.md) keeps its own human title and names its task in the
34	// machine block's first line, so the id comes from the task whose worker path that
35	// is. `pathTo` is that lookup, injected because only the run holds the task set.
36	export const taskIdOf = (item, pathTo = () => null) => {
37	  const p = parseWorkItemTitle(item.title);
38	  if (p) return `${p.pack}/${p.task}`;
39	  return pathTo(parseWorkItemBody(item.body).taskPath) ?? null;
40	};
41	
42	// The pick order (PRINCIPLES.md): urgent first, then RANDOM among the ready, with
43	// two skip rules read live at pick time. Random rather than oldest-first because
44	// nothing leans on FIFO aging — the stale-ready escalation is period-scale — while
45	// a deterministic order lets one unlucky head dominate every run of a chain
46	// (PRINCIPLES.md).
47	//
48	//  - SAME-TITLE MUTEX (S15/F6): skip an item whose exact title has another open
49	//    item executing or handed to an agent — one task, one execution at a time,
50	//    while a fan-out's distinct qualifiers still parallelize.
51	//  - THE `after` YIELD (S23): skip a scheduled item whose task declares `after:
52	//    [T]` while T's standing item is live THIS CYCLE (ready / executing / agent).
53	//    A declined upstream holds nothing back — it has no item at all (a no files
54	//    nothing, PRINCIPLES.md) — and neither does one sitting `needs-human`: a broken
55	//    upstream must not halt its dependents indefinitely.
56	//
57	// `open` is every open work item; `taskAfter(id)` gives a task's declared
58	// upstreams as `<pack>/<task>` ids, and `scheduledOf(id)` whether that task is
59	// asked by the scheduler at HEAD (`isScheduledTask`; null where the repo no longer
60	// carries it) — which is half of what says whether an item is a standing
61	// occurrence or an ad-hoc run (PRINCIPLES.md). `random` is the tie-break draw, injected
62	// so a test can pin an order the production call deliberately does not have.
63	export function pickOrder(open = [], { taskAfter = () => [], scheduledOf = () => null, random = Math.random, pathTo = () => null } = {}) {
64	  const idOf = (item) => taskIdOf(item, pathTo);
65	  const live = (item) => [STATUS_READY, STATUS_RUNNING_EXECUTOR, STATUS_RUNNING_AGENT].some((s) => isStatus(item, s));
66	  const standing = (item) => isStandingItem(item, scheduledOf(idOf(item)));
67	  const liveUpstream = (upstreamId) => open.some((o) =>
68	    idOf(o) === upstreamId && standing(o) && live(o));
69	  // One draw per item, taken once: a comparator that called `random()` per
70	  // comparison would not be a consistent ordering, and `Array.sort` on one is
71	  // free to produce anything at all.
72	  const draw = new Map(open.map((i) => [i.number, random()]));
73	
74	  return open
75	    .filter((i) => isStatus(i, STATUS_READY))
76	    .filter((i) => !open.some((o) => o.number !== i.number && titleOf(o) === titleOf(i)
77	      && running(o)))
78	    .filter((i) => {
79	      if (!standing(i)) return true;
80	      return !taskAfter(idOf(i)).some(liveUpstream);
81	    })
82	    .sort((a, b) =>
83	      (hasLabel(b, URGENT) ? 1 : 0) - (hasLabel(a, URGENT) ? 1 : 0)
84	      || draw.get(a.number) - draw.get(b.number));
85	}
86

1	# verify-production — coded production validations
2	
3	The queue's coded verification lane (#1530). A change whose proof lives at a URL — a
4	Pages site, a deployed config, a published module — cannot be verified by an agent
5	session, which has no egress. This task is the runner for those: the verification
6	issue carries declarative probes, and the worker fetches and judges them as
7	code-work, Action-side, where egress exists.
8	
9	The filing form — when to file one at all, and the brief's fields — is the basics
10	pack's [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md)
11	skill. An issue routes here by naming `Task: claudinite-tasks/verify-production`
12	beside its mark.
13	
14	## The spec the worker reads
15	
16	Parsed from the human half of the issue body by [`probes.mjs`](probes.mjs), which
17	is also where the assertion grammar is defined and documented:
18	
19	```
20	Original-issue: #<n>
21	Task: claudinite-tasks/verify-production
22	Live-probe: <url> :: <assertion>
23	Verify-probe: <url> :: <assertion>
24	Retry-every: <count> <minutes|hours|days|weeks>
25	```
26	
27	Both probe classes are required, and the difference is the whole design: a failing
28	`Live-probe:` means the release has not landed (re-arm and come back), a failing
29	`Verify-probe:` — judged only once liveness passes — means a real fault in
30	production. Without the gate the two are indistinguishable, and a verify failure
31	would reopen the original issue over a release that simply has not happened.
32	
33	## The four verdicts
34	
35	- **invalid** — the spec is unreadable: the worker exits non-zero with a triage
36	  marker naming every problem, and the item parks.
37	- **not yet live** — the worker prints the `claudinite-requeue:` marker with
38	  now + `Retry-every:` and exits clean; the executor re-arms the item's
39	  `Not-before` and returns it to blocked.
40	- **pass** — the evidence actually read is commented on the item; the executor
41	  closes it done.
42	- **fail** — `Original-issue:` is reopened with what was asserted and what was
43	  read; the item links it and closes done — the verification did its job by
44	  finding the fault.
45	
46	## Watching a fresh one fail
47	
48	A coded run costs seconds, so a new verification should be watched failing before
49	its release lands: dispatch the scheduler workflow (its `workflow_dispatch`), and
50	the adoption-plus-drain executes the probes immediately. The run reporting
51	**not yet live** is the see-it-fail proof — the probes execute and do not pass
52	vacuously — and the same item then flips on its own once the release is live.
53	
54	## Why the declaration reads as it does
55	
56	Carried over from the declaration's comments when it became `task.json`.
57	
58	The coded production-validation task (#1530). A verification issue that names
59	this task (`Task: claudinite-tasks/verify-production`) carries declarative URL
60	probes; the worker fetches and judges them as code-work — Action-side, where
61	egress exists — so no agent session is ever spent, and no egress wall is ever
62	hit. The grammar and the verdict flow are the worker's (see README.md beside
63	it); the filing form is the basics pack's verify-in-production skill.
64	
65	MANUAL: an item exists only because a verification was filed and marked —
66	there is nothing to put on a calendar.
67	A filed production verification is its own mandate.
68	A handful of bounded HTTP fetches plus a few issue writes — minutes at most.

1	// Agent invocation (docs/PRINCIPLES.md). The executor starts the
2	// agent session with an API CALL rather than by arming a label event, which is
3	// what retires the re-arm, the grace window and the transport dance — and what
4	// makes a lost hand-off a synchronous, visible failure at the executor instead of
5	// a label event fired into the void.
6	//
7	// A TASK NAMES AN ENDPOINT, NEVER A URL. The declaration is vendored verbatim
8	// into every consuming repo, so it must never carry deployment detail or anything
9	// adjacent to a credential: `invocation_endpoint: 'fleet'` names a key, and the
10	// repo's own config maps that key to a URL and to the NAME of the repo Actions
11	// secret holding its token. That indirection is also what replaces the whole
12	// self/fleet apparatus — reach is a property of which endpoint you call, so a
13	// task needing wider access names a different endpoint and nothing else in the
14	// system needs a concept of scope.
15	//
16	// THE PROMPT NAMES ONE ITEM AND CARRIES NO INSTRUCTIONS. Everything
17	// behavior-defining is read by the session from the tracked task files at HEAD;
18	// the prompt says which issue and which nonce, and the session validates both in
19	// code before acting (PRINCIPLES.md).
20	
21	import { ENDPOINTS_KEY } from '../../../../engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs';
22	import { secretValue } from './secrets-bag.mjs';
23	
24	export const DEFAULT_ENDPOINT = 'default';
25	
26	// The endpoint is a ROUTINE'S API TRIGGER — `POST /v1/claude_code/routines/
27	// <trigger-id>/fire` with a per-routine bearer token — which is what Claude Code
28	// on the web actually exposes to an HTTP caller. Three consequences the design's
29	// "a CCR API call" did not spell out, each verified against the routines docs
30	// rather than assumed:
31	//
32	//  - THE BEHAVIOR IS THE ROUTINE'S STORED PROMPT, not ours. `text` reaches the
33	//    session wrapped in a `<routine-fire-payload>` block explicitly labelled
34	//    untrusted, and a routine acts on it only because its own saved prompt says
35	//    to. That is the issue-is-data posture arriving for free at one more hop: our
36	//    payload names an item, and every instruction comes from a stored artifact.
37	//    The routine's stored prompt is one line pointing at `instructions.md` beside
38	//    this file, so the whole of what a session does is tracked and reviewed.
39	//  - THE BODY CARRIES ONE FIELD. `text` is freeform and unparsed — structured
40	//    JSON would arrive as a literal string — so the item number and nonce go in
41	//    as prose, and nothing else goes in at all.
42	//  - THERE IS NO IDEMPOTENCY KEY (standing entry 11, answered: the endpoint
43	//    offers none), which is exactly why THIS MODULE CALLS ONCE PER ITEM AND NEVER
44	//    RETRIES. A retry is only safe when you know the first call did nothing, and
45	//    a client-side timeout is the one case where you cannot know — the session
46	//    may well have started. Retrying there is what would make invocation
47	//    at-least-once and put two sessions on one item; declining to retry is what
48	//    keeps it at-most-once and lets the whole agent-side claim protocol delete.
49	//    An outcome we did not learn is reported as UNKNOWN and resolved by the agent
50	//    leash, which is a rule that already exists, rather than by a guess here.
51	//
52	// The beta header is dated and the endpoint is a research preview whose two most
53	// recent header versions keep working, so it lives in config with a default here
54	// — a rotation is then a config edit on one repo, never an engine release the
55	// whole fleet waits for.
56	export const DEFAULT_HEADERS = Object.freeze({
57	  'anthropic-beta': 'experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01',
58	  'anthropic-version': '2023-06-01',
59	});
60	
61	// The endpoint a task's hand-off calls, resolved against the repo's config.
62	// Returns `{ name, url, tokenEnv, headers }` or `{ name, error }` — a task naming
63	// an endpoint the repo has not configured is a repo-configuration fact, reported
64	// where the operator reads it, never a crash.
65	export function resolveEndpoint(config, task) {
66	  const name = task?.decl?.invocation_endpoint ?? DEFAULT_ENDPOINT;
67	  const endpoints = config?.taskScheduler?.[ENDPOINTS_KEY] ?? {};
68	  const entry = endpoints[name];
69	  if (!entry) {
70	    return { name, error: `this repo's settings declare no invocation endpoint "${name}" (taskScheduler.${ENDPOINTS_KEY})` };
71	  }
72	  if (!entry.url) return { name, error: `invocation endpoint "${name}" declares no url` };
73	  if (!entry.tokenSecret) return { name, error: `invocation endpoint "${name}" declares no tokenSecret (the NAME of the repo Actions secret holding its token)` };
74	  return { name, url: entry.url, tokenEnv: entry.tokenSecret, headers: { ...DEFAULT_HEADERS, ...(entry.headers ?? {}) } };
75	}
76	
77	// The fire payload: which item, and the nonce that proves this call is the one
78	// the hand-off comment recorded. Prose, not JSON — the field is freeform and
79	// unparsed, so a structured payload would arrive as a literal string — and
80	// deliberately free of instructions, because the routine's stored prompt is what
81	// says how to act on it (see `instructions.md`). The session still validates
82	// the item in code before touching it: a payload labelled untrusted is trusted no
83	// more than a label event was.
84	export const firePayload = ({ repo, item, nonce }) =>
85	  `Claudinite work item: ${repo}#${item.number}. Invocation nonce: ${nonce}.`;
86	
87	// The invoker seam the executor calls, exactly once per item. Failure is DATA,
88	// never a throw, and it comes in two kinds the caller must treat differently:
89	//
90	//   { ok: true, sessionId, sessionUrl }   the routine fired; a session exists
91	//   { ok: false, answered: true, error }  the endpoint ANSWERED and refused —
92	//                                         no session, and the cause is a
93	//                                         configuration fault a retry cannot fix
94	//   { ok: false, answered: false, error } no answer reached us — a timeout, a
95	//                                         dropped connection. The session may or
96	//                                         may not exist, and nothing here may
97	//                                         guess which.
98	export function agentInvoker({ repo, config, env = process.env, fetchImpl = fetch, timeoutMs = 60e3 }) {
99	  return async function invoke({ task, item, nonce }) {
100	    const endpoint = resolveEndpoint(config, task);
101	    // A configuration fault, decided before any call: definite, and no session.
102	    if (endpoint.error) return { ok: false, answered: true, error: endpoint.error };
103	    const token = secretValue(endpoint.tokenEnv, env);
104	    if (!token) {
105	      // The `code_work_required_secrets` posture, applied to the endpoint token: nothing
106	      // fails silently, the task just doesn't work yet, and the item names what to
107	      // fix (PRINCIPLES.md).
108	      //
109	      // WHAT WAS OBSERVED, AND BOTH CAUSES. The first version asserted "the secret
110	      // is not set in this repo", which this code cannot see: on the member that
111	      // wedged in #1296 the secret was set the whole time and the executor workflow
112	      // simply never passed it. The reader believed the message, went to the Secrets
113	      // page, found it present, and had nowhere to go next.
114	      return { ok: false, answered: true, error: `\`${endpoint.tokenEnv}\`, the token for invocation endpoint "${endpoint.name}", is empty in this job. Either the repository secret is not set, or \`.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml\` does not pass it — check that this repo's executor workflow names it under the \`# claudinite:secrets\` marker — a workflow whose list has not caught up with the endpoint's \`tokenSecret\` is the usual cause, and only a human-merged PR moves that file` };
115	    }
116	
117	    const payload = { text: firePayload({ repo, item, nonce }) };
118	
119	    // ONE call. No loop, and deliberately no `attempts` knob for anyone to raise.
120	    try {
121	      const res = await fetchImpl(endpoint.url, {
122	        method: 'POST',
123	        headers: {
124	          ...endpoint.headers,
125	          'content-type': 'application/json',
126	          authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
127	          'user-agent': 'claudinite-executor',
128	        },
129	        body: JSON.stringify(payload),
130	        signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs),
131	      });
132	      let json = null;
133	      try { json = await res.json(); } catch { json = null; }
134	      if (res.status >= 200 && res.status < 300) {
135	        return {
136	          ok: true,
137	          sessionId: json?.claude_code_session_id ?? null,
138	          sessionUrl: json?.claude_code_session_url ?? null,
139	        };
140	      }
141	      // A status came back, so the endpoint decided: no session was started, and
142	      // the cause is a token, a URL or a routine — none of which a retry fixes.
143	      return {
144	        ok: false, answered: true,
145	        error: `endpoint "${endpoint.name}" returned ${res.status}${json?.error ? `: ${JSON.stringify(json.error)}` : ''}`,
146	      };
147	    } catch (e) {
148	      // Nothing came back. The request may have landed and started a session, so
149	      // this is the one outcome that must never be retried and never be reported

1	# implement-request
2	
3	## Why the declaration reads as it does
4	
5	Carried over from the declaration's comments when it became `task.json`.
6	
7	The request implementer (docs/PRINCIPLES.md) — the engine's one built-in
8	task, and the only one that may read an item's `Model`.
9	
10	A person marks an ordinary issue `task:origin:ad-hoc`; the scheduler run adopts
11	it by writing the machine block onto that issue and applying the first status —
12	the issue IS the item (PRINCIPLES.md); this task's precondition decides, at pickup,
13	whether the run happens; the session implements the issue and leaves a pull
14	request. There is no code-work phase at all: the authorization a worker would
15	have performed is the precondition's, and the item's `Request:` field — which
16	names the item's own issue — is the whole payload.
17	The literal, not the constant beside it in `built-in-tasks.mjs`: the
18	declaration-shape check reads this file statically and cannot resolve an
19	import. The two are pinned to each other in request-mode.test.mjs.
20	MANUAL: the scheduler run never puts this on a calendar. An item exists only because an
21	issue was marked, which is what makes a request a first-class origin of work
22	rather than a schedule nobody asked for.
23	The security check, in preconditions.mjs beside this file. It judges the ONE
24	issue this item names — the `Request:` field — which is why the term reads the
25	item rather than a window of repo activity.
26	The default when the asker named no family; the item's `Model:` overrides it,
27	and only because this task declares the field below.
28	The ceiling the executor enforces in code. The task's own policy is the full
29	`anything` because the REAL decider is per-request: the asker's `Automerge:`
30	becomes the item's `Merge:` field (PRINCIPLES.md), a policy expression the worker
31	hands to the policy engine, and the task ceiling must not sit below whatever
32	an asker may legitimately authorize. A ceiling is a maximum, not an
33	instruction: with no such field the worker opens a pull request and parks at
34	the approval lane exactly as every request did before, and with one it still
35	parks whenever the policy engine says the diff is not covered.
36	A run that died mid-flight leaves a branch, a PR, or neither, and only a person
37	can say whether the half-done work stands — so nothing re-queues it mechanically.
38

1	// Is a default-branch commit GENUINE PROJECT WORK, or the machinery moving? The one
2	// test, published because two very different readers ask it: the signal collectors,
3	// which gate a precondition on whether the repo moved in a window, and a cross-repo
4	// reader (the dashboard) deciding whether a member looks quiet. A second notion of
5	// "meaningful" would mark a member sleepy on the very commits its own scheduler counts
6	// as movement.
7	//
8	// Import-light and free of `node:` on purpose, like dormancy.mjs: the dashboard reads
9	// this in the browser through the pack's published public/.
10	
11	import { taskFromMessage } from '../../public/work-item-grammar.mjs';
12	
13	// Bot/CI housekeeping and Claudinite's own automated writes, by MESSAGE. The queue's
14	// own vocabulary (`[claudinite-task]`, `[claudinite-work]`) is excluded here so
15	// neither dispatch mechanism ever self-triggers: a queue-mode repo's work items are
16	// repo activity to every precondition watching issues.
17	export const HOUSEKEEPING = /\[skip ci\]|(^|\n)\s*baselin(e|ing)\b|claudinite[ -](baselin|maintenance|growth|task|work)|seed default-on/i;
18	
19	// The exclusion the message cannot express: a commit that touched nothing outside
20	// `.claudinite/` moved the repo's own working rules, not the project. Every consumer
21	// means "genuine project work" by this — something shippable changed (store-release),
22	// there is a lesson to extract (growth-extract), a comment may have drifted
23	// (improve-comments) — and none of those is true of a corpus edit. Message and author
24	// cannot catch it: a human landing a lesson PR writes an ordinary message under their
25	// own login, so the growth lifecycle's own landed output re-armed it the next night
26	// and a repo could never go quiet (TLDR #319).
27	//
28	// An empty list is UNKNOWN, never "touched only .claudinite/" — a bare `every` is
29	// vacuously true on it and would silently retire the trigger for every commit whose
30	// detail read failed. Require at least one known path before the exclusion applies.
31	const CORPUS_ONLY = (files) => files.length > 0 && files.every((f) => f.startsWith('.claudinite/'));
32	
33	// The test. `files` is the commit's changed paths where the caller resolved them, and
34	// `null` where it did not: a reader working from a commit LISTING has no file list and
35	// cannot afford a read per commit, so it gets the author, trailer and message
36	// exclusions and states that the corpus-only one did not run. The trailer is the
37	// AUTHORITY for anything written after it existed — a commit a scheduled task wrote
38	// says so itself — and the message and author exclusions stay because history
39	// predating the trailer still needs classifying and because they also cover
40	// non-task housekeeping.
41	export function isSubstantiveCommit(commit, files = null) {
42	  const login = commit?.author?.login ?? commit?.author ?? '';
43	  if (typeof login === 'string' && login.endsWith('[bot]')) return false;
44	  const message = commit?.commit?.message ?? commit?.message ?? '';
45	  if (taskFromMessage(message)) return false;
46	  if (files !== null && CORPUS_ONLY(files)) return false;
47	  return !HOUSEKEEPING.test(message);
48	}
49

1	// The executor's repository-variable bag (#1492).
2	//
3	// WHY THIS EXISTS. Actions requires a workflow to name each value it passes, so
4	// before this a task needing a repo variable needed the executor workflow to name it —
5	// and `.github/workflows/` is the one path an update cannot write, so that meant a
6	// human-merged PR in every member, the coupling that wedged one in #1296. One static
7	// line, `CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}`, ends it: the workflow stops being a
8	// function of what any task declares, and setting a variable in repo settings is the
9	// whole of adding one.
10	//
11	// WHY THE SECRETS BAG CANNOT DO THE SAME. `toJSON(secrets)` is the shape GitHub's
12	// malicious-workflow detection flags (#1336): the run parks with zero jobs until a
13	// person clicks Approve, silently and fleet-wide. `vars` is not that shape. It is the
14	// context GitHub's own docs define as non-sensitive and render UNMASKED in build logs,
15	// so serialising it exfiltrates nothing the logs do not already show, and vendored
16	// site-deploy workflows have passed `toJSON(vars)` since before that safeguard
17	// shipped without a single park. GitHub publishes no detection signals, so
18	// this is inference plus our own field evidence rather than a guarantee; if it is ever
19	// wrong the symptom is #1336's — `action_required` with zero jobs, which reads exactly
20	// like an idle queue.
21	
22	import { parseBag } from './env-bag.mjs';
23	import { actionsEnv } from './actions.mjs';
24	
25	export const VARS_BAG_ENV = 'CLAUDINITE_VARS';
26	
27	export const varsBag = (env = actionsEnv()) => parseBag(env[VARS_BAG_ENV]);
28	
29	// The bag as an environment fragment: what a task's code-work should gain, and nothing
30	// it should lose.
31	//
32	// ADDITIVE, NEVER OVERWRITING — the one place this deliberately differs from the
33	// secrets bag, which wins over a same-named plain variable. That bag replaced named
34	// lines and is subtracted from the inherited environment before it is applied, so it
35	// has nothing to collide with. This one is applied ON TOP of a live runner environment
36	// it does not own, and a repository variable is any name an owner typed into a settings
37	// box. A repo with a variable called `PATH` or `HOME` must not be able to reach into a
38	// task subprocess and replace the runner's own; anything already present came from the
39	// runner or from the workflow, both of which are more specific than "every variable
40	// this repository happens to define". For a variable the workflow ALSO names, the two
41	// values come from the same context and are identical, so nothing is lost by yielding.
42	//
43	// A missing or malformed bag contributes nothing, which is also the shape of the window
44	// a member spends between this engine converging and its own executor workflow landing.
45	export function varsEnv(env = actionsEnv()) {
46	  const bag = varsBag(env);
47	  if (!bag) return {};
48	  const out = {};
49	  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(bag)) {
50	    // Otherwise one variable re-exports the whole blob under its own name.
51	    if (name === VARS_BAG_ENV) continue;
52	    if (env[name] !== undefined) continue;
53	    out[name] = value;
54	  }
55	  return out;
56	}

1	// The dispatch issue — how a due (task, slot) becomes exactly-once, bounded,
2	// recoverable agent work (docs/PRINCIPLES.md). This module is the
3	// PURE half: issue identity (title/body/parse) and the create / skip / suppress
4	// decision over the issues that already exist. A thin scheduler shell does the
5	// GitHub I/O (search state=all, create, label, comment) and applies the verdict
6	// — the "should I file this" decision is always code here, never the shell's
7	// judgment (the same split the fleet planner uses).
8	//
9	// All behavior-defining content (agent_model, expected_outcome, agent_instructions) is read from the
10	// tracked task files, never from the issue — the body only points at the task
11	// file and carries the precondition's binding Context (PRINCIPLES.md).
12	import { NEEDS_HUMAN } from '../../public/task-constants.mjs';
13	
14	
15	// The labels this machinery drives. `ready-for-agent` is what the executor
16	// routine fires on; `needs-human` is the single triage state every anomaly
17	// converges to (PRINCIPLES.md lifecycle). Kept here as the shared source for the
18	// scheduler side; the executor reuses these plus `agent-running`.
19	export const READY_LABEL = 'ready-for-agent';
20	// Fleet-scoped work dispatches to a DISTINCT ready label so a separate,
21	// broader-scoped executor routine runs it - keeping the fleet-wide session grant
22	// off every ordinary project's self executor (the per-project-scheduling fleet/self
23	// split).
24	export const READY_FLEET_LABEL = 'ready-for-agent-fleet';
25	export const AGENT_RUNNING_LABEL = 'agent-running';
26	export { NEEDS_HUMAN };
27	export const WORKFLOW_FAILURE_LABEL = 'workflow-failure';
28	
29	// WHICH EXECUTOR ROUTINE a session is. Not a property of a task - nothing asks a
30	// task what its reach is (a task needing more than its own repo names an
31	// `invocation_endpoint`) - but of the routine that is running: an ordinary
32	// project's executor is `self`, the broader-scoped fleet routine is `fleet`, and
33	// each picks up only what is filed under its own ready label.
34	export const EXECUTOR_SCOPES = ['self', 'fleet'];
35	
36	// The ready label a dispatch is filed under, from the scope of the executor meant
37	// to run it ('self' default → READY_LABEL; 'fleet' → READY_FLEET_LABEL). The one
38	// place this mapping lives, so the scheduler (which files) and any reader stay in
39	// sync.
40	export const readyLabelForScope = (scope) => (scope === 'fleet' ? READY_FLEET_LABEL : READY_LABEL);
41	
42	// The full label set the scheduler + executor drive, each with the colour and
43	// description a bootstrap one-off would have given it. The scheduler ENSURES every
44	// one exists (create-if-missing, idempotent) right before it dispatches — so there
45	// is no separate label-creation step to run or forget, and a deleted label
46	// self-heals on the next run. This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: GitHub does not
47	// create a label when you apply it (the issues API 422s on an unknown label), so
48	// the thing that assigns a label must guarantee it first — the
49	// gha/label-create-before-add principle, enforced in code here.
50	export const SCHEDULER_LABELS = [
51	  { name: READY_LABEL, color: '0e8a16', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: dispatch issue ready for the (self-scoped) executor to run' },
52	  { name: READY_FLEET_LABEL, color: '1d76db', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: dispatch ready for the FLEET-scoped executor (a task reaching other repos)' },
53	  { name: AGENT_RUNNING_LABEL, color: 'fbca04', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: the executor has claimed this issue and is running it' },
54	  { name: NEEDS_HUMAN, color: 'd93f0b', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: an anomaly that converged here for human triage' },
55	  { name: WORKFLOW_FAILURE_LABEL, color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' },
56	];
57	
58	// The escalation code as a LABEL, so "which condition woke the agent" is countable
59	// rather than only readable. The body already names the code, but a body is prose:
60	// counting it across a fleet means fetching and parsing every dispatch issue, while a
61	// label is a search facet (`label:escalation:checks-not-green`) any repo-set query can
62	// aggregate — which is what sizing the versioned-updates pack-apply stage needs (#768,
63	// the versioned-updates design, PRINCIPLES.md).
64	//
65	// DERIVED from the code the worker fired, never a list of codes kept here: the codes
66	// live in the code-work worker that raises them (a pack), the engine may not import a
67	// pack, and a hand-maintained copy of an enum on the other side of that barrier is
68	// exactly the drift the corpus forbids. So the label is minted per code, and the
69	// scheduler ensures it right before applying it — the same create-before-add
70	// discipline SCHEDULER_LABELS documents. A code that is not a plain kebab-case token
71	// gets no label (GitHub would take almost anything as a name, and a label built from
72	// a malformed code is a category nobody can query); the body still carries it.
73	export const ESCALATION_LABEL_PREFIX = 'escalation:';
74	export function escalationLabel(code) {
75	  if (typeof code !== 'string' || !/^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/.test(code)) return null;
76	  return {
77	    name: `${ESCALATION_LABEL_PREFIX}${code}`,
78	    color: '5319e7',
79	    description: `Claudinite scheduler: code_work escalated on "${code}"`,
80	  };
81	}
82	
83	// Title: `[claudinite-task] <pack>/<task> <slot-id>` (PRINCIPLES.md). The prefix is
84	// what keeps these issues invisible to the scheduler's own signals (self-trigger
85	// exclusion) and searchable as a family.
86	export const DISPATCH_PREFIX = '[claudinite-task]';
87	
88	export const dispatchTitle = ({ pack, task, slotId }) => `${DISPATCH_PREFIX} ${pack}/${task} ${slotId}`;
89	
90	// The (pack, task) family key — every slot's title for one task starts with
91	// `<key> ` (the trailing space before the slot id is load-bearing: it stops
92	// `foo/extract` from matching `foo/extract-more`).
93	export const dispatchTaskKey = ({ pack, task }) => `${DISPATCH_PREFIX} ${pack}/${task}`;
94	
95	// pack and task ids are single path segments (no slash, no space); the slot id
96	// is the trailing non-space token.
97	const DISPATCH_TITLE_RE = /^\[claudinite-task\]\s+([^/\s]+)\/([^/\s]+)\s+(\S+)$/;
98	
99	export function parseDispatchTitle(title) {
100	  const m = DISPATCH_TITLE_RE.exec(String(title ?? '').trim());
101	  return m ? { pack: m[1], task: m[2], slotId: m[3] } : null;
102	}
103	
104	// Is this a scheduler dispatch issue? The self-trigger exclusion the signal
105	// collectors apply so the scheduler never sees its own dispatch issues as work.
106	export const isDispatchTitle = (title) => parseDispatchTitle(title) !== null;
107	
108	// The dispatch issue body (PRINCIPLES.md). First line is the task-file path — the
109	// only thing the executor reads to locate the worker; everything below is human
110	// framing plus the precondition's binding Context. The Context block is emitted
111	// only when the precondition produced lines (an empty scope has nothing to bind).
112	// The `### Delivered` section — what this run's code-work created, by identity. It is
113	// the agent's only source for those artifacts.
114	//
115	// Absence is meaningful: no section means code-work created nothing, so never write a
116	// placeholder here.
117	export function deliveredLines(delivered) {
118	  const { branch = null, pr = null, merged = false } = delivered ?? {};
119	  if (!branch && !pr) return [];
120	  return [
121	    '### Delivered by code-work',
122	    'The artifacts this run created — the ones to work on.',
123	    '',
124	    ...(pr ? [`- PR: #${pr}${merged ? ' (already merged — open your own PR for further work)' : ' (open)'}`] : []),
125	    ...(branch ? [`- Branch: \`${branch}\``] : []),
126	  ];
127	}
128	
129	// The `### Why the agent is here` section — which of code-work's escalation
130	// conditions fired. The worker knows it exactly; without this the agent re-derives it
131	// from the repo, and a re-derivation that disagrees with the truth is how a run ends up
132	// reporting "code-work created nothing" about a cycle that just merged a PR
133	// (EdFringeAllocator#82).
134	//
135	// The condition and its counts, never the findings — those stay in the repo (PRINCIPLES.md).
136	// Absence is meaningful here too: a worker too old to name a reason says nothing, and
137	// the agent falls back to its task file's own sweep.
138	export function escalationLines(reason) {
139	  const { code = null, detail = null } = reason ?? {};
140	  if (!code && !detail) return [];
141	  return [
142	    '### Why the agent is here',
143	    'The condition code_work escalated on. Start here; the findings themselves are in the repo, not this issue.',
144	    '',
145	    `- ${detail || code}${detail && code ? ` (\`${code}\`)` : ''}`,
146	  ];
147	}
148	
149	export function dispatchBody({ taskPath, pack, task, slotId, context = [], delivered = null, reason = null }) {
150	  const lines = [taskPath, ''];
151	  if (context.length) {
152	    lines.push(
153	      `Execute the Claudinite task above (pack \`${pack}\`, task \`${task}\`, slot \`${slotId}\`).`,
154	      'The Context section below is binding scope — do not re-decide it.',
155	      '',
156	      '### Context',
157	    );
158	    for (const c of context) lines.push(`- ${c}`);
159	  } else {
160	    lines.push(`Execute the Claudinite task above (pack \`${pack}\`, task \`${task}\`, slot \`${slotId}\`).`);
161	  }
162	  // Why first, then what: the reason is what decides which of the task file's sections
163	  // the agent actually needs, and the artifacts are what it does that work on.
164	  const why = escalationLines(reason);
165	  if (why.length) lines.push('', ...why);
166	  const del = deliveredLines(delivered);
167	  if (del.length) lines.push('', ...del);
168	  return lines.join('\n') + '\n';
169	}
170	
171	// The filing decision for one due (task, slot), given `existing` — the issues
172	// the shell fetched for this task's family (title starts with the task key),
173	// each `{ number, title, state, labels }` with state 'open' | 'closed'. Two
174	// guards (PRINCIPLES.md):
175	//   - exactly-once per (task, slot): a state=all title match for THIS slot → skip
176	//     (makes double-runs and crash-retries safe).
177	//   - at-most-one-LIVE per task: an open family issue that is still live work
178	//     suppresses a new filing → an executor outage accumulates at most one issue
179	//     per task.
180	// Otherwise: create (the shell files it labeled with `readyLabel` — the
181	// self/fleet ready label the task's scope resolves to, default `ready-for-agent`).
182	//
183	// LIVE, NOT MERELY OPEN (#821). Suppressing on any open issue read `needs-human`
184	// as live work, so an escalation did not await triage — it STOPPED the task until
185	// a person closed the issue by hand, with nothing saying the lane was shut. That
186	// made the stale-claim backstop the opposite of a backstop: it converted one
187	// session's death into a permanent stop (13 tasks across 9 repos, the oldest
188	// stopped for three weeks). A claim — `agent-running`, or a just-filed issue not
189	// yet labeled — is someone working; a terminal is nobody, and never will be.
190	//
191	// The re-filing is bounded, because a DURABLE cause escalates every slot and would
192	// otherwise accumulate one issue per slot — the spam the guard exists to prevent.
193	// One unresolved escalation is a transient session death and must not cost the
194	// task its next slot; a second says the cause outlived a full cycle of triage, so
195	// the lane holds until a person drains it. That hold is a distinct verdict
196	// (`escalated`), not the claim verdict, so "a session is on it" and "shut,
197	// pending triage" can never again look identical from outside.
198	export const NEEDS_HUMAN_HOLD = 2;
199	
200	// GitHub hands labels back as objects on the issues/search APIs and as bare
201	// strings in some fixtures; accept either.
202	const labelNames = (issue) =>
203	  (issue?.labels ?? []).map((l) => (typeof l === 'string' ? l : l?.name)).filter(Boolean);
204	
205	const isEscalated = (issue) => labelNames(issue).includes(NEEDS_HUMAN);
206	
207	export function planDispatch({ existing = [], pack, task, slotId, readyLabel = READY_LABEL, hold = NEEDS_HUMAN_HOLD }) {
208	  const title = dispatchTitle({ pack, task, slotId });
209	  const keyPrefix = `${dispatchTaskKey({ pack, task })} `;
210	  const family = existing.filter((i) => `${(i.title ?? '').trim()} `.startsWith(keyPrefix));
211	
212	  if (family.some((i) => (i.title ?? '').trim() === title)) {
213	    return { action: 'skip', reason: `dispatch issue for slot ${slotId} already exists (exactly-once)` };
214	  }
215	  const open = family.filter((i) => i.state === 'open');
216	  const live = open.find((i) => !isEscalated(i));
217	  if (live) {
218	    return { action: 'suppress', openIssue: live.number, reason: `an open dispatch issue (#${live.number}) already covers ${pack}/${task}` };
219	  }
220	  const escalated = open.filter(isEscalated);
221	  if (escalated.length >= hold) {
222	    const numbers = escalated.map((i) => `#${i.number}`).join(', ');
223	    return {
224	      action: 'suppress', escalated: true, openIssue: escalated[0].number,
225	      reason: `${escalated.length} unresolved escalations (${numbers}) on ${pack}/${task} — held for triage, not running`,
226	    };
227	  }
228	  return { action: 'create', title, label: readyLabel, reason: `no dispatch issue yet for ${pack}/${task} slot ${slotId}` };
229	}
230	
231	// The period one slot id represents, from its leading kind char (h/d/w/m). Used
232	// only for the stale-issue backstop's threshold; daily-family slots all span a
233	// day. Monthly uses 31 days so the ~2-period threshold never fires early in a
234	// long month.
235	const SLOT_PERIOD_MS = { h: 3600e3, d: 86400e3, w: 7 * 86400e3, m: 31 * 86400e3 };
236	
237	function slotPeriodMs(slotId) {
238	  return SLOT_PERIOD_MS[String(slotId ?? '')[0]] ?? null;
239	}
240	
241	// Open dispatch issues older than `factor` of their own period (PRINCIPLES.md: ~2
242	// periods) — the scheduler's backstop when no executor session drains them. The
243	// shell adds the escalation comment + `needs-human` to each. `issue.created_at`
244	// is the ISO string GitHub returns; a title that doesn't parse (or an unknown
245	// slot kind) is never stale here.
246	//
247	// ESCALATION IS ONCE. Escalating only adds a label and leaves the issue OPEN, so
248	// an issue that already carries `needs-human` still matches every later run —
249	// and the shell re-posts the identical comment on each. Skipping the already
250	// escalated is what makes "converge to a single visible state" true rather than
251	// a state the scheduler keeps re-announcing every hour, forever.
252	//
253	// A CLAIMED issue is not this sweep's to judge either. `agent-running` means a
254	// session engaged; whether that claim is dead is `staleClaimedDispatchIssues`'s
255	// question, and it says so in its own words. Without this the two overlap on an
256	// old claimed issue, the shell's stale-first ordering wins, and the issue is
257	// told "no executor session ran it" about a session that demonstrably ran.
258	export function staleDispatchIssues(openIssues = [], now, { factor = 2 } = {}) {
259	  const nowMs = new Date(now).getTime();
260	  return openIssues.filter((issue) => {
261	    const parsed = parseDispatchTitle(issue.title);
262	    if (!parsed) return false;
263	    const names = labelNames(issue);
264	    if (names.includes(NEEDS_HUMAN) || names.includes(AGENT_RUNNING_LABEL)) return false;
265	    const period = slotPeriodMs(parsed.slotId);
266	    if (period === null) return false;
267	    return nowMs - new Date(issue.created_at).getTime() > factor * period;
268	  });
269	}
270	
271	// The escalation comment the shell posts on a stale dispatch issue.
272	export function staleEscalationComment(issue) {
273	  const parsed = parseDispatchTitle(issue.title);
274	  const which = parsed ? `${parsed.pack}/${parsed.task} (slot ${parsed.slotId})` : 'this task';
275	  return `This dispatch issue for ${which} has stayed open past ~2 of its scheduling periods without being executed — `
276	    + `no executor session ran it. Labeling \`${NEEDS_HUMAN}\` for triage.`;
277	}
278	
279	// --- re-arming a lost trigger ------------------------------------------------
280	// The label event is the executor's ONLY trigger, and a delivery can be lost: the
281	// routine was down or paused, or a session died before it claimed. The issue then
282	// sits armed forever, because the label is already applied and GitHub emits
283	// `labeled` only on a fresh add. So the scheduler re-arms it — remove the ready
284	// label, add it back — which emits a new event.
285	//
286	// This is the recovery that used to live in the executor's drain sweep, then in
287	// the scheduler's own pass, where it runs again as the repair phase -
288	// still deterministic code, still decided by the pure rules here. The sweep had EVERY triggered session also process every
289	// OTHER armed issue, so one scheduler run filing N dispatches produced N sessions
290	// each racing over the same N issues, and the claim swap could not stop it (every
291	// session read the work list before any claim landed). That is the
292	// duplicate-execution bug: the same dispatch run two or three times over,
293	// duplicate tracker issues, duplicate PRs making the same changes. Recovery
294	// belongs here, where it is a decision in code that runs once per scheduler run.
295	
296	const READY_LABELS = new Set([READY_LABEL, READY_FLEET_LABEL]);
297	
298	// The ready label an issue currently carries, or null. Re-arming reapplies THIS
299	// one, so a fleet dispatch is never re-armed as a self dispatch (which would hand
300	// it to an executor whose session lacks the cross-repo reach it needs).
301	export function readyLabelOn(issue) {
302	  return labelNames(issue).find((n) => READY_LABELS.has(n)) ?? null;
303	}
304	
305	// The open dispatch issues whose trigger evidently never landed. Re-arm only an
306	// issue that is:
307	//   - a dispatch issue (parseable title) still carrying a ready label;
308	//   - unclaimed — no `agent-running` (a live session claims before it dispatches)
309	//     and not already converged to `needs-human`;
310	//   - uncommented — the executor comments on every exit path, so a comment means
311	//     some session engaged and this is not a lost event; and
312	//   - past `graceMs` (default 20m), comfortably beyond session spin-up, so a
313	//     session already on its way is never handed a rival.
314	// A stale issue is never re-armed: it is on its way to `needs-human`, and re-arming
315	// one would loop forever.
316	//
317	// NOTHING CALLS THIS ANY MORE. The slot scheduler it belonged to is retired (#974)
318	// and the sweep that ran these rules went with the janitor task. They are kept pure
319	// and tested as the shape a legacy-cleanup rule takes, for the home named in
320	// `../schedule/repair.mjs`; a caller would read the items that pass already holds.
321	// Dispatch issues left claimed by a session that died mid-run: `agent-running`
322	// with no activity for `idleMs` (~3h). Converging these used to be the executor's
323	// own step 6, which meant every concurrently-triggered session swept them and
324	// commented on the same issue — the duplicate-work bug in miniature. It is code
325	// here, beside the re-arm and uncalled for the same reason.
326	//
327	// Scoped to `[claudinite-task]` dispatch issues deliberately (the title parse is
328	// what enforces it): a task may put `agent-running` on an issue IT owns — a
329	// request its pipeline has claimed, which stays claimed while its PR is in review,
330	// far longer than 3h — and only that task knows when its own claim is stale.
331	//
332	// SILENCE IS THE HOLDER'S, NOT THE ISSUE'S (#924). `livenessAt` is the shell's read
333	// of when the session that holds this claim last signed for it — its own claim or
334	// heartbeat comment, `lastLivenessAt` in `../items/heartbeat.mjs`. Measuring from
335	// `updated_at` instead reads a dead claim as live, because any comment moves it: a
336	// losing executor letting go, a person, the task's own bookkeeping. `updated_at` is
337	// still the fallback, for an issue with no liveness signal at all and for a comment
338	// read that did not answer — a read that fails is not a verdict that the holder is
339	// dead.
340	export function staleClaimedDispatchIssues(openIssues = [], now, { idleMs = 3 * 3600e3 } = {}) {
341	  const nowMs = new Date(now).getTime();
342	  return openIssues.filter((issue) => {
343	    if (!parseDispatchTitle(issue.title)) return false;
344	    const names = labelNames(issue);
345	    if (!names.includes(AGENT_RUNNING_LABEL) || names.includes(NEEDS_HUMAN)) return false;
346	    const lastSign = issue.livenessAt ?? issue.updated_at ?? issue.created_at;
347	    return nowMs - new Date(lastSign).getTime() > idleMs;
348	  });
349	}
350	
351	// The claims a sweep must read comments for before it can judge them -
352	// `livenessAt`'s scope. Every open dispatch claim, so a candidate set narrowed by
353	// the very clock the rule stopped trusting cannot narrow it wrongly; the count is
354	// the health line's `running`, a handful.
355	export const claimedDispatchIssues = (openIssues = []) => openIssues.filter((issue) => {
356	  if (!parseDispatchTitle(issue.title)) return false;
357	  const names = labelNames(issue);
358	  return names.includes(AGENT_RUNNING_LABEL) && !names.includes(NEEDS_HUMAN);
359	});
360	
361	// The comment the shell posts when it reclaims a dead session's claim.
362	export function staleClaimComment(issue) {
363	  const parsed = parseDispatchTitle(issue.title);
364	  const which = parsed ? `${parsed.pack}/${parsed.task} (slot ${parsed.slotId})` : 'this task';
365	  return `This dispatch issue for ${which} has carried \`${AGENT_RUNNING_LABEL}\` for over 3h with no activity — `
366	    + `the executor session that claimed it never converged it. Labeling \`${NEEDS_HUMAN}\` for triage.`;
367	}
368	
369	export function rearmDispatchIssues(openIssues = [], now, { graceMs = 20 * 60e3 } = {}) {
370	  const nowMs = new Date(now).getTime();
371	  const stale = new Set(staleDispatchIssues(openIssues, now).map((i) => i.number));
372	  return openIssues.filter((issue) => {
373	    if (!parseDispatchTitle(issue.title)) return false;
374	    if (stale.has(issue.number)) return false;
375	    if (!readyLabelOn(issue)) return false;
376	    const names = labelNames(issue);
377	    if (names.includes(AGENT_RUNNING_LABEL) || names.includes(NEEDS_HUMAN)) return false;
378	    if ((issue.comments ?? 0) > 0) return false;
379	    return nowMs - new Date(issue.created_at).getTime() > graceMs;
380	  });
381	}
